Subject: Re: CS handoff: model lane decisions & hourly traffic profile

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the samples, very helpful. Draft thoughts below to guide the implementation planning doc (I included Ben and Kim for capacity and quant recommendations).

1) Model lanes:
- Chat (user-facing conversational flow): recommend a medium-size open model in the 8B–13B range quantized to 4-bit for cost-sensitive prod. Rationale: your examples have frequent back-and-forth with mid-length context (~800–1,200 tokens). We can fallback to a smaller 4B opt variant for very low-latency endpoints.
- Embeddings (search/retrieval & similarity): use a dedicated embedding model (128–512-d vectors) with batching and async ingestion. Separate GPU pool to avoid contention.

2) Context length:
- Primary chat window: plan for up to 2,048 tokens. Sample prompts average ~900 tokens; allow headroom for user history.
- System prompts / long docs pipeline: for doc-attach flows, we should support up to 8k window via retrieval + chunking (we'll recommend rerank/shortlist to keep live tokens low).

3) Traffic bands (initial estimate) — Ben can confirm but rough bands for sizing:
- Peak hours (14:00–18:00 UTC): 45% of daily requests
- Mid hours (09:00–14:00 UTC / 18:00–23:00 UTC): 35%
- Off-peak (23:00–09:00 UTC): 20%

Next steps: Ben — can you drop an hourly token profile CSV and indicate recommended dedicated GPU pool size for steady and burst? Kim — please add quantization and batch config we should prescribe in the onboarding playbook.

Thanks,
Grace
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightline.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:33:00Z
Subject: Re: CS handoff: model lane decisions & hourly traffic profile

Quick pass with numbers attached (traffic_hourly_estimate.csv). Key assumptions called out in the CSV. TL;DR recommendations:
- Steady-state: 2x GPUs (A100-40C equivalent) pooled for chat lanes to handle baseline QPS with batching (target tail p95 token latency < 250ms); this assumes 8B quantized model with 4-bit and continuous batching.
- Burst headroom: reserve a 1.5x burst pool (autoscale to 3x for top 1% daily peak).
- Embeddings: single V100-class machine with high-throughput batching; ingestion can be offloaded to a dedicated queue.

Attachments: traffic_hourly_estimate.csv — columns: UTC_hour, est_requests, est_tokens_per_request, est_total_tokens. I included a conservative and optimistic column.

Notes: if Brightline pushes for 8k live windows for a subset of flows, we need to plan for extra KV-cache memory and route those requests to a different model variant to avoid increasing cost on conversational lane.

—Ben
Staff Engineer, Performance & Cost Modeling, Redwood Inference

This looks great — thanks everyone. I reviewed the CSV and the suggested pools align with our cost model. A couple of clarifications before the implementation runbook is finalized: 
- Can you add an explicit fallback policy in the runbook for model degradation (e.g., auto-fallback to the 4B opt variant and reduced context during sustained >95th percentile latency)?
- For embeddings: what's your recommendation for batch windows to balance latency vs throughput for our search API (SLA target 150ms)?

I've attached the sample prompts (brightline_sample_prompts.txt) and added a short doc with a few long-form prompts that will hit the 2k–6k window (we flagged them for chunking). Let's set a 30-minute sync Thursday to lock the runbook and rollout plan.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Product Lead, Brightline
